messages:
riz: hey team quick Q  planning an IVF cycle next month. Clinic says meds will be ~ $4k before insurance. Does Redwood Choice PPO cover fertility meds and IVF procedures? Any tips to reduce OOP or prior auth nuances?

sara (People Ops): hi riz  short: coverage varies by state and specific plan. Many medical benefits cover fertility meds partially or via the pharmacy benefit; IVF procedural coverage is limited for many employers. For Redwood Choice PPO: some meds are covered under pharmacy benefits with prior authorization; IVF procedures may be covered if there's a medical diagnosis and prior auth. DM me your plan member ID and clinic paperwork and well check specifics.

riz: thanks. clinic gave me a treatment plan and a med list (injectables + oral). They said some meds are billed as medical (J codes) and some as pharmacy (NDC). How to figure what gets billed where?

sara (People Ops): good question. Injectables given in clinic are often billed under medical (J codes) and could be processed as medical benefit; self-administered injectables filled at specialty pharmacy are pharmacy benefit. Ask clinic to provide CPT/HCPCS and NDCs on the estimate. If a med is billed under medical, it may apply to medical deductible/copay; if pharmacy, it follows pharmacy deductible/coinsurance.

benefits-bot: automated note  Prior auth tips: 1) ask clinic to submit a procedure-level prior auth for IVF cycle (if they provide it), 2) submit medication prior auths to PBM for specialty injectables, 3) keep all itemized estimates and authorize start date windows. Typical auth turnaround: meds 3-7 days, procedures 5-10 days.

anna: vendor tip  some clinics will set up a patient assistance or manufacturer copay card for certain injectable meds which can dramatically reduce OOP. Also ask if the clinic will bill meds through clinic vs. external specialty pharmacy; clinic-billed meds sometimes count toward medical OOP, which may be better depending on your deductible.

riz: ok. if pharmacy benefit covers some meds, will prior auth go through our PBM or the insurer?

sara (People Ops): PBM handles pharmacy prior auths; insurer handles medical prior auths. For meds with split billing, you might get two separate auths. When you submit to PBM, have prescribers NPI, ICD diagnosis, and prior auth paperwork ready. If your clinic offers to coordinate, ask them to run benefits and submit auths for both sides.

pharmacy-team: from pharmacy side  if you send us the NDCs and prior auth forms, we can estimate patient responsibility and check manufacturer copay programs. If a specialty pharmacy is needed, they can often set up 2-4 week starter fills while auth completes. Share the med list and we'll look up coverage rules.

riz: any short template I can send the clinic and the specialty pharmacy so we don't miss docs?

sara (People Ops): yes - copy/paste below.

```
Subject: Prior Auth & Coverage Check  IVF Cycle Meds and Procedure

Hi [Clinic / Pharmacy],

Member: Riz Lastname | DOB: [MM/DD/YYYY] | Member ID: [########]
Plan: Redwood Choice PPO (Group: [######])
Treatment: IVF stimulation cycle starting [MM/DD/YYYY]

Please submit the following for benefit verification and prior authorization:
1) Itemized estimate with CPT/HCPCS codes for procedures and J-codes if clinic-billing meds.
2) Medication list with NDCs for pharmacy-billed injectables and oral meds.
3) Clinical notes supporting medical necessity (diagnosis: [ICD-10]).
4) Prior auth requests to insurer (procedures) and PBM (pharmacy meds).

Please send authorizations/estimates to [riz@email.com] and upload to insurer/PBM portal. If any meds have manufacturer copay assistance, please include enrollment instructions.

Thanks,
Riz
```

benefits-bot: reminder  keep receipts for any interim payments and track whether charges post to medical or pharmacy OOP. If you hit a denial, save the denial EOB and forward to people-ops@redwood.com and we can assist with appeals or asking clinic to rebill under the correct benefit.

riz: great, sending to clinic now. sara  i'll DM my member ID and med list. thanks all!
